html:
Eastern Roman emperor from 610 to 641, whose reign saw both a great victory and a great loss. His father, the governor of Africa, sent him with a fleet against the hated emperor Phocas, whom he overthrew in 610.

He came to power in the middle of the last great war with Persia. The armies of Khosrow II took Syria, Jerusalem with the relic of the True Cross, and Egypt. From 622 Heraclius struck back by leading armies deep into Persian lands. Constantinople held out against the Avar and Persian siege of 626, and in 627 he won near Nineveh. Persia made peace, and he brought the Cross back to Jerusalem in 630.

Within a few years the Arab conquests undid it. After the defeat at the Yarmuk in 636 he lost Syria, and Egypt fell soon after his death. His attempt to unite the church through the Ecthesis failed. Greek replaced Latin as the language of government in his time, and the empire that remained is often called Byzantine from here on.
sum: Eastern Roman emperor from 610 to 641, whose reign saw both a great victory and a great loss. His father, the governor of Africa, sent him with a fleet against the hated emperor Phocas, whom he overthrew in 610.
